conviction_note: Modal outcome is an in-line-to-slightly-better Q1 and a reaffirmed 5-6% FY27 guide into a stock already down 9.79% in 20 days on a hiring-freeze narrative that Paychex's own published client-employment index says did not hit the reported quarter; that is a relief move, not a numbers move, which is why the reaction (+1.0) is sized above the fundamental read (+0.5). It is held to about one point rather than the three-to-four a clean reaffirm could pay, because the direction I reach is the same direction the sealed baseline already states twice for free — a -9.79% run-up and a -3.33 skew with upside paid — and because this name's own last print beat revenue and EPS and fell 2.3%, so its reaction function does not pay for the quarter.
bar: Q1 FY27 consensus revenue $1.63bn and adjusted EPS $1.32 (18 analysts, EPS range $1.29-$1.34, revenue range $1.62-1.63bn) per https://pluang.com/en/news-feed/laporan-pendapatan-paychex-payx-t1-2027-dan-perkiraan, agreeing with $1.32 at https://news.alphastreet.com/paychex-payx-q1-2027-preview-eps-est-1-32-reports-september-23/, and cross-checked against the company's own FY27 guide of 5-6% total revenue growth in the 2026-06-24 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000723531/000119312526280314/payx-ex99_1.htm). $1.63bn against $1.54bn a year ago is +5.8%, i.e. the street is modelling Q1 at the TOP of the company's own full-year range. Two agreeing estimate sources plus a company guide, so no size cap is applied.
positioning_check: Short interest 6.40% of float, 8.89 days to cover, 20.42m shares short and building from 19.24m (stockanalysis.com/stocks/payx/statistics/, read 2026-09-22 via the sweep row). That is an elevated and rising short base for a $41bn mega-cap and nearly nine days of cover. The sealed baseline's 25-delta skew is -3.33 vol points — NEGATIVE, i.e. upside is paid over downside, the most negative in the day's universe — with put/call open interest of 0.41. Both the skew and the free control (-run_up_20d_pct of -9.79%) point the same way as my findings, which is the reason the emitted number is small rather than large: I am largely agreeing with information the baseline gives away. The crowded short is the reason my one negative finding was shrunk rather than sized full.

findings.finding: Paychex's FY2027 guidance, set 2026-06-25, explicitly assumes 'no further changes to the Fed funds rate' and on that basis guides interest on funds held for clients DOWN to $195-205m from FY2026's $210.9m; the Fed then HIKED 25bp on 2026-09-16 to 3.75-4.00%, its first increase since 2023, with the dot plot at 4.00-4.25% for both year-end 2026 and 2027 and markets pricing a further hike.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the exact line the stock trades on. On 2026-06-24 PAYX beat on both revenue (+12%) and adjusted EPS ($1.32) and fell 1.72% purely because the FY27 guide — of which this interest line was a named drag — sat below the street's ~8%. On 2025-06-25 the FY26 guide took the stock down 9.4%. The baseline's seven reactions are 4 down / 3 up with a 1.72% median, and the down days are guide days.
findings.why_not_priced: PAYX fell over the five sessions spanning the 16 September hike (sealed run_up_5d_pct -3.91%), so the market read a hiking Fed purely as a small-business demand negative and did not mark up a ~100%-margin float line that the company had guided down on an assumption the hike has now falsified. If this were priced, PAYX would have outperformed payroll peers after 16 September and the client-funds line would appear in the previews; the previews are entirely about hiring freezes. The dollars are deliberately sized small: per the 31 Aug 2025 10-Q the float is $4.98bn available-for-sale against only $775.2m of money-market and restricted cash equivalents, so ~86% of the portfolio reprices on the ladder rather than with Fed funds, making the direct FY27 benefit roughly $2-5m of a $195-205m line. What is worth more than the dollars is that a guided line gets revised the right way on a day the market is braced for the wrong way.
findings.independence: The FOMC decision itself is a separate primary source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/16/fed-rate-decision-september-2026.html (2026-09-16). ADP set its own FY27 interest assumptions off 'Fed Funds futures contracts and various forward yield curves as of July 28, 2026' (https://mediacenter.adp.com/2026-07-29-ADP-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-2026-Results), so the whole payroll-float complex is carrying a pre-hike rate assumption, not just Paychex. NOTE: this finding shares the client-funds line with finding 3 below; they are the forward and the trailing leg of the same line and are deliberately signed opposite, not double-counted.

findings.finding: Paychex publishes its own free monthly Small Business Employment Watch, and it covers exactly the June-August quarter about to be reported: June 2026 printed a jobs index of 99.83, the highest since August 2025 and a fourth consecutive monthly improvement, and August printed 99.13, in line with the 2026 year-to-date average of 99.20, with weekly hours growth positive for a sixth straight month — so the 'flat employment levels' assumption underpinning the FY27 guide held through the reported quarter even as the stock lost 9.79% in 20 days on hiring-freeze fear.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Filed as guidance rather than reported_quarter deliberately: on 2026-06-24 this name beat both reported lines and still fell 2.3%, and the sweep row states a reported-quarter beat here is worth close to zero. What this series actually settles is reaffirm-versus-cut on the annual guide, and the guide is what moved the stock -1.72% in June 2026 and -9.4% in June 2025. The counterweight is resolved inside this finding rather than left to argue against it: the index deteriorated WITHIN the quarter, from 99.83 in June to roughly 99.23 in July to 99.13 in August, so the data supports a guide that is reaffirmed and does NOT support one that is raised. Paychex has historically reaffirmed rather than raised at Q1 in any case. That is why this is sized at +0.7 and not at the +1.4 a clean reading of the quarter alone would have carried.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown has a named cause and it is a large-cap narrative, not this company's book: PAYX fell 3.9% in a single session on 2026-09-08 on fears that corporate hiring freezes would spread to small business. If the market were weighting Paychex's own client-base index over that narrative, the stock could not have fallen 3.9% in a session in the month after its own index printed a twelve-month high for the first month of the quarter being reported. The August release is at https://www.stocktitan.net/news/PAYX/stable-employment-levels-continue-for-u-s-small-businesses-in-k2eaefz17ugv.html (2026-09-01). Sized modestly because this is a free company press release on an 18-analyst, $41bn name — the opposite of the thin-coverage setup where an unpriced fact moves a stock hard.
findings.independence: ADP, a direct competitor measuring the same client base, guided US pays per control to 0% to 1% for its FY27 on 2026-07-29 (https://mediacenter.adp.com/2026-07-29-ADP-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-2026-Results) — consistent with flat, not contracting. Cutting the other way, and stated rather than hidden: ADP's National Employment Report put small businesses under 50 employees at just +3,000 jobs in August with total private payrolls +38,000, the smallest since January (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/02/private-payrolls-rose-by-38000-in-august-fewer-than-expected-adp-reports.html). That is the exit-rate weakness already priced into the +0.7.

findings.finding: The Q1 consensus revenue bar of $1.63bn is +5.8% year on year, sitting at the very top of the company's own 5-6% full-year guide, in the single quarter of FY27 carrying the hardest interest-on-funds comparison: Q1 FY26 interest was $47.6m and grew 27% on the Paycor balance step-up, struck with Fed funds at 4.25-4.50% against 3.50-3.75% through this quarter, and the Paycor balance benefit has now lapped.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The directly comparable event is the last Q1 print, 2025-09-30, which moved -1.38%. Q1 is the print at which this company reaffirms rather than raises, so a revenue line that merely matches a top-of-guide bar has historically not been rewarded. Across the baseline's seven reactions the median absolute move is 1.72% and four of seven are negative.
findings.why_not_priced: The street's Q1 number is published and the company's annual range is published, but the arithmetic between them — that consensus requires top-of-range growth in the quarter with the largest embedded rate headwind and no remaining acquisition inflation — is not in any preview I found, which all frame the quarter as a hiring-freeze question. If it were priced, the Q1 revenue estimate would sit nearer the middle of the guided range rather than at its ceiling.
findings.independence: Shares the client-funds line with finding 1 and rests on the same 8-K/10-Q family; it is the trailing-comparison leg where finding 1 is the forward-guide leg, and the two are signed opposite on purpose rather than summed as independent evidence. Shrunk from -0.6 to -0.4 because 8.89 days to cover and a -3.33 skew make a crowded short a mechanism against any negative here.

outside_window.finding: Paychex's own September 2026 Small Business Employment Watch — the first read on whether the September hiring-freeze deterioration reached Paychex's client book, and the real test of the 'flat employment' guidance assumption — publishes around 2026-10-01, after the exit window closes.

The next FOMC meeting in late October 2026; markets price a further 25bp hike and the dot plot sits at 4.00-4.25%, which would break Paychex's 'no further changes to the Fed funds rate' assumption a second time and further lift the client-funds line above the $195-205m guide.

searched_and_found_nothing: Insider buying: no open-market (code P) Form 4 purchases in September 2026 — the only September filing found was a 334-share gift disposition by B. Thomas Golisano on 2026-09-01. No insider conviction signal into a 13% drawdown from the high.

Capital return catalyst at this print: Paychex raises its dividend in April/May (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and most recently to $1.19 from $1.08), not in September, and the $1bn buyback authorization dates from 2026-01-16 with ~$389m still unspent. Nothing new is due on 09-23.

Paycor integration distress: searched for attrition, layoffs and restructuring and found the opposite — ~$100m of expense synergies largely complete, revenue synergies tracking to the high end of the 30-50bp target, and employee attrition better than Paycor's own history.
Executive change: no CFO or senior leadership 8-K in September 2026; Bob Schrader remains CFO.

Peer read-through for a negative: Paycom raised FY26 guidance in early August and Paylocity guided FY27 revenue to ~7% growth on 2026-08-04. No HCM peer has flagged a small-business volume break since Paychex last spoke.

PEO/insurance loss-ratio blowout: looked for evidence that medical and workers-comp inflation is compressing the PEO take rate; found only generic medical-inflation commentary and management calling medical inflation a PEO tailwind. No company-level number to size.

The FY2026 10-K's quantitative Item 7A rate-sensitivity table, which would have let finding 1 be sized in dollars rather than bounded — the document is too large to retrieve that section through the available fetchers.
baseline_tension: It agrees with both, and that is the main reason the number is small: the -3.33 skew says upside is paid and the -9.79% run-up is the stage's own free control pointing the same way, so two-thirds of my direction is already given away by the sealed file, and what I add is only the mechanism (a falsified rate assumption and the company's own quarter-coincident employment index) rather than the sign.
lessons_applied: S1 and S2 — re-labelled the Employment Watch finding from `reported_quarter` to `guidance` and cut it from +1.4 to +0.7: this name beat revenue and EPS on 2026-06-24 and fell 2.3%, so the reported quarter is not the line it pays for, and what the index actually settles is reaffirm-versus-cut on the annual guide.

S3 — resolved the contradiction inside finding 2 instead of leaving it in `independence` to argue against its own number: the index went 99.83 in June to ~99.23 in July to 99.13 in August, so the data supports a reaffirm and refutes a raise, and that resolution is now the reason for the size rather than a footnote under it.

S8 inverts on this name and pulled every size down — an 18-analyst, $41bn mega-cap whose key series is its own free monthly press release is the opposite of the thin-coverage setup in which a confirmed fact moves a stock hard; the pre-lessons draft had implicitly borrowed that lesson's upward pressure without qualifying for it.

S2 — re-sized the broken Fed-assumption finding on its actual dollars rather than its narrative, +0.9 to +0.6, after establishing from the 10-Q that $4.98bn of the $5.75bn float is available-for-sale and only $775.2m is money-market, so 25bp of Fed funds is worth roughly $2-5m of a $195-205m guided line.
S7 — shrank the negative bar finding from -0.6 to -0.4 on 8.89 days to cover and a rising 6.40% short base, because a crowded short is a mechanism of its own against a negative.

S7 also kept the skew and short interest OUT of `findings` and in `positioning_check` where they belong; the pre-lessons draft had already declined to file them as a fourth finding, and the file confirmed that call.

S6 left the bar standing — two agreeing estimate sources plus the company's own 5-6% guide — so no size cap was applied, and the observation that consensus sits at the ceiling of the guided range became the basis of finding 3 rather than a caveat.
Net effect: impact sum +1.7 to +0.9, emitted move +1.7 to +1.0, print_vs_bar +0.6 to +0.5. The file moved the sizes and one `lands_on` label; it did not remove a finding or change a sign.
